name: Shakti side test (10 min per side): amygdala signal
summary: Murphy's side test before any one-sided series: 10 min of the amygdala signal over the right temporal lobe, where he says it is usually unpleasant, then at once 10 min at the mirror site on the left. It checks for what Murphy calls a 'reversed' structure. The vendor's file is not published; the signal is rebuilt from the published point count and point length.
setting: Quiet, dim room, eyes closed, relaxed. One coil above each ear: T8 (right) for phase 1 and T7 (left) for phase 2; the other six stay unused. Note how each half feels: pleasant, unpleasant or nothing.
schedule: One signal per test and at most one test every 72 hours (vendor rule).
notes: The vendor: 'To test a signal, apply it over the side that's usually UNPLEASANT for that signal', for ten minutes, 'followed immediately by the same signal over the same location on the other side of the head'; it also allows 'between 5 and 10 minutes on each side' (testsession.htm). This program plays 10 min on the right (T8), then 10 min on the left (T7), one coil per side; Skip ends a side early. T7/T8 and one coil per side are this project's choices: if a one-sided series will use other sites, test there. The amygdala signal is the project's rising sweep (6 to 30 Hz) with the published point duration and length (230 points of 3 ms, Ryczko 2002 p.1 [592]); the point values were never published as numbers (the lab prints the shape only as a small figure). Each sweep is followed by 4 s of silence, as the vendor describes; the lab papers give 4 s from start to start. Field strength: the vendor's test pages state none. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Murphy reads a response opposite to the usual one as a sign of a 'reversed' or 'left-handed' structure, and says: 'If you get no response at all, you probably do not have one'. His side rule rests on user reports and one small Persinger-lab study, where burst-firing fields over the right temporal lobe raised apprehension in women. That study used 70 to 90 mG over the stimulated side (Richards 1992 p.2 [668]), far more than any Shakti figure. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Murphy links the right amygdala with fear and sadness, so the first half can bring fear: press Skip to move on. Negative imagery is his sign that a session has run too long. Not for people with epilepsy, seizure history or a psychiatric condition; stop on distress.
